response.headline: Distance to the nearest mast is the likely cause [distance_to_mast].

causes.explanation: The nearest confirmed mast is 4.8 km away and only O2 has sites within 5 km [nearest_site][operators_5km], while Vodafone is 9.5 km away with a weak line-of-sight margin [los_vodafone]. O2, EE and Three all have clear lines of sight to nearer sites [los_o2][los_ee][los_three][network_comparison], so distance alone is not a strong blocker.
No Ookla speed tests exist within 1 km, in this cell, or in any neighbouring cell in 2026Q3 [speed_1km][speed_cell][speed_neighbours], so actual signal quality at the point cannot be measured.

actions.text: Try O2 as the likely best network here [network_comparison].
Use Wi-Fi calling indoors if signal is weak.
Check the address on Ofcom's mobile coverage checker: https://www.ofcom.org.uk/mobile-coverage-checker
Emergency calls work on any available network.

response.best_network: O2 is likely best, with a clear line of sight to a confirmed site 4.8 km west [network_comparison]. EE and Three also have clear lines of sight to confirmed sites 5.6 km east [los_ee][los_three][network_comparison]. Vodafone's site is 9.5 km south, inferred rather than confirmed, with a weak line-of-sight margin [los_vodafone].
limitations: Sites are approximate; antenna heights assumed; Ofcom figures are area-level.
Causes are inferred from public data, not confirmed: operators' network data is not public.
Ookla speeds are quarterly aggregates with no time-of-day detail; congestion can only be inferred.
No address-level Ofcom coverage; Ofcom figures are for the whole constituency and are predictions.
Mast sites are approximate (crowd-sourced OpenCelliD, OpenStreetMap, Ofcom's licence register) and incomplete, so 'no sites found' is weak evidence.
Line of sight uses a surface model (trees and buildings included) and mostly assumed antenna heights; blocked means a weaker signal, not no signal.
